import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Perfect komi

We model Go on a $19 \times 19$ board with area scoring. Black moves first, suicide is forbidden,
positional superko prevents repetition of a board position, and two consecutive passes end the
game. Empty regions bordered by both colours, including shared liberties in seki, score for neither
player.
The perfect komi is the minimax value of Black's final score margin.

*References:*

- [Wikipedia, Komi (Go)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komi_%28Go%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
-/

namespace Komi

/-- The two stone colours. -/
inductive Color
  | black
  | white
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The colour that plays after `c`. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .black => .white
  | .white => .black

abbrev Point := Fin 19 × Fin 19
abbrev Board := Point → Option Color

/-- Orthogonal adjacency on the Go board. -/
def Adjacent (p q : Point) : Prop :=
  (p.1.val + 1 = q.1.val ∧ p.2 = q.2) ∨
  (q.1.val + 1 = p.1.val ∧ p.2 = q.2) ∨
  (p.2.val + 1 = q.2.val ∧ p.1 = q.1) ∨
  (q.2.val + 1 = p.2.val ∧ p.1 = q.1)

instance : DecidableRel Adjacent := fun p q => by
  unfold Adjacent
  infer_instance

/-- Two points are connected through points on which `b` has the value `x`. -/
def Connected (b : Board) (x : Option Color) (p q : Point) : Prop :=
  b p = x ∧ b q = x ∧
    Relation.ReflTransGen (fun u v => Adjacent u v ∧ b u = x ∧ b v = x) p q

/-- The chain containing `p` has a liberty. -/
def HasLiberty (b : Board) (p : Point) : Prop :=
  ∃ q r, Connected b (b p) p q ∧ Adjacent q r ∧ b r = none

/-- Put a stone on a board, before removing captured stones. -/
def place (b : Board) (c : Color) (p : Point) : Board :=
  Function.update b p (some c)

/-- The board after placing a stone and simultaneously removing every adjacent enemy chain
without a liberty. -/
noncomputable def afterMove (b : Board) (c : Color) (p : Point) : Board := by
  classical
  let b' := place b c p
  exact fun q =>
    if b' q = some c.other ∧ ∃ r, Adjacent p r ∧ Connected b' (some c.other) r q ∧
        ¬ HasLiberty b' r then none
    else b' q

/-- A state records the current board, all earlier board positions, the player to move, and the
number of consecutive passes. -/
structure State where
  board : Board
  history : Finset Board
  turn : Color
  passes : ℕ

/-- An action is either a pass (`none`) or placement at a board point (`some p`). -/
abbrev Action := Option Point

/-- Legality of an action. Stone placement requires an empty point, must not be suicide after
captures, and must not repeat an earlier board position. -/
def Legal (s : State) : Action → Prop
  | none => True
  | some p =>
      s.board p = none ∧
      afterMove s.board s.turn p p = some s.turn ∧
      HasLiberty (afterMove s.board s.turn p) p ∧
      afterMove s.board s.turn p ∉ s.history

/-- Update the state by a legal action. -/
noncomputable def play (s : State) : Action → State
  | none => ⟨s.board, s.history, s.turn.other, s.passes + 1⟩
  | some p =>
      let b := afterMove s.board s.turn p
      ⟨b, insert b s.history, s.turn.other, 0⟩

/-- The finite collection of legal actions from a state. -/
noncomputable def legalActions (s : State) : Finset Action := by
  classical
  exact Finset.univ.filter (Legal s)

/-- An empty point is territory of `c` when its entire connected empty region has a stone of colour
`c` on its boundary and no stone of the other colour there. -/
def Territory (b : Board) (c : Color) (p : Point) : Prop :=
  b p = none ∧
  (∃ q r, Connected b none p q ∧ Adjacent q r ∧ b r = some c) ∧
  ∀ q r, Connected b none p q → Adjacent q r → b r ≠ none → b r = some c

/-- Area points belonging to a colour: its stones together with its surrounded territory. -/
noncomputable def area (b : Board) (c : Color) : ℕ := by
  classical
  exact (Finset.univ.filter fun p => b p = some c ∨ Territory b c p).card

/-- Black's area score minus White's area score. -/
noncomputable def score (b : Board) : ℤ :=
  area b .black - area b .white

/-- Maximum of a list, with a value for the empty list. -/
def listMax (fallback : ℤ) : List ℤ → ℤ
  | [] => fallback
  | x :: xs => max x (listMax fallback xs)

/-- Minimum of a list, with a value for the empty list. -/
def listMin (fallback : ℤ) : List ℤ → ℤ
  | [] => fallback
  | x :: xs => min x (listMin fallback xs)

/-- Backward induction for Go. Black maximizes and White minimizes the final Black score margin.
The fuel is immaterial when it exceeds twice the number of board positions: superko allows each
board position at most once, and between two placements there can be at most one pass. -/
noncomputable def gameValue : ℕ → State → ℤ
  | 0, s => score s.board
  | n + 1, s =>
      if s.passes ≥ 2 then score s.board
      else
        let outcomes := (legalActions s).toList.map fun a => gameValue n (play s a)
        match s.turn with
        | .black => listMax (score s.board) outcomes
        | .white => listMin (score s.board) outcomes

/-- The empty board. -/
def emptyBoard : Board := fun _ => none

/-- The perfect komi: Black's final score margin under perfect play from an empty 19 by 19 board. -/
noncomputable def perfectKomi : ℤ :=
  let initial : State := ⟨emptyBoard, {emptyBoard}, .black, 0⟩
  gameValue (2 * Fintype.card Board + 2) initial

/--
The perfect value of komi is 7 points: under perfect play on a $19 \times 19$ board with the area
scoring and positional-superko rules fixed above, adding 7 points to White's score produces jigo.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 5 91]
theorem komi : perfectKomi = 7 := by
  sorry

end Komi
modeling_decisions: Interpreted the candidate answer in the background article and fixed decomposition literally: the conjecture is that perfect komi is 7 points, rather than leaving the requested value as `answer(sorry)`.

Fixed a concrete ruleset because perfect komi is ruleset-dependent: a 19×19 board, Black first, alternating play, orthogonal chains and liberties, simultaneous capture of adjacent enemy chains, suicide forbidden, positional superko, and termination after two consecutive passes.

Used area scoring: each colour receives one point for each of its stones and for each empty point in a connected empty region whose nonempty boundary consists only of that colour. A region with no stone boundary (including the initial empty board) belongs to neither colour, and mixed-boundary/shared seki liberties belong to neither colour.

Modeled perfect play by finite backward induction: Black maximizes and White minimizes Black's integer area-score margin. Positional superko bounds placements by the number of boards, and at most one nonterminal pass can occur between placements, so fuel `2 * Fintype.card Board + 2` exceeds every legal play length.
Defined perfect komi as Black's final score margin, since adding exactly that amount to White's score makes the adjusted scores equal (jigo).

Did not impose a separate `NoSeki` restriction. The article invokes absence of seki to explain the odd-integer observation, while presenting 7 as the candidate perfect value; the chosen area-scoring predicate directly handles shared seki regions neutrally.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Komi

Komi in the game of Go are points added to the score of the player with the white stones as
compensation for playing second. A *perfect* value of komi would make each game end in a draw
(jigo) under perfect play by both sides. Under area scoring the perfect komi is an integer
(Black's final score minus White's final score under perfect play), and statistics from
professional and computer play suggest that its value on the standard `19 × 19` board is `7`.

This file models Go with the Tromp–Taylor rules (area scoring, positional superko, suicide
allowed, game over after two consecutive passes), defines the value of the game under perfect
play, and asks for its value on the `19 × 19` board.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Komi (Go)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komi_%28Go%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)
- [J. Tromp, B. Taylor, The Logical Rules of Go](https://tromp.github.io/go.html)
-/

namespace Komi

open SimpleGraph

/-- The two colours of stones, which also name the two players. -/
inductive Color
  | black
  | white
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The opponent's colour. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .black => .white
  | .white => .black

/-- A point of the `n × n` grid. -/
abbrev Point (n : ℕ) := Fin n × Fin n

/-- Two points of the grid are adjacent if they are horizontally or vertically next to each
other, i.e. adjacent in the box product of two path graphs. -/
abbrev grid (n : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Point n) := pathGraph n □ pathGraph n

/-- A grid colouring: each point is empty (`none`) or carries a stone of some colour. -/
abbrev Position (n : ℕ) := Point n → Option Color

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- In the position `pos`, the point `p` *reaches* the colour `c` (where `none` stands for
"empty") if there is a path of adjacent points, all coloured like `p`, from `p` to a point adjacent
to a point coloured `c`. -/
def Reaches (pos : Position n) (p : Point n) (c : Option Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ q r, Relation.ReflTransGen (fun a b => (grid n).Adj a b ∧ pos b = pos p) p q ∧
    (grid n).Adj q r ∧ pos r = c

open scoped Classical in
/-- *Clearing* the colour `c` empties every point of colour `c` that does not reach an empty
point. -/
noncomputable def clear (pos : Position n) (c : Color) : Position n :=
  fun p => if pos p = some c ∧ ¬ Reaches pos p none then none else pos p

/-- The position obtained when the player `c` plays at the point `p`: `p` is coloured `c`, then
the opponent's colour is cleared, then the player's own colour is cleared. -/
noncomputable def play (pos : Position n) (c : Color) (p : Point n) : Position n :=
  clear (clear (Function.update pos p (some c)) c.other) c

/-- The (area) score of the player `c` in the position `pos`: the number of points coloured `c`
plus the number of empty points that reach `c` but not the opponent's colour. -/
noncomputable def score (pos : Position n) (c : Color) : ℕ :=
  Nat.card {p : Point n // pos p = some c} +
    Nat.card {p : Point n //
      pos p = none ∧ Reaches pos p (some c) ∧ ¬ Reaches pos p (some c.other)}

/-- The result of a finished game in the position `pos`: Black's score minus White's score. -/
noncomputable def result (pos : Position n) : ℤ :=
  score pos .black - score pos .white

/-- The state of a game of Go in progress. -/
structure State (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The current grid colouring. -/
  pos : Position n
  /-- The player whose turn it is. -/
  toMove : Color
  /-- All grid colourings that have occurred so far, including the current one. -/
  history : Finset (Position n)
  /-- Whether the previous turn was a pass. -/
  lastPass : Bool

namespace State

/-- The initial state: an empty board, Black to move. -/
def initial (n : ℕ) : State n where
  pos := fun _ => none
  toMove := .black
  history := {fun _ => none}
  lastPass := false

/-- The state after the player to move passes. -/
def pass (s : State n) : State n :=
  { s with toMove := s.toMove.other, lastPass := true }

/-- The state after the player to move plays at the point `p`. -/
noncomputable def move (s : State n) (p : Point n) : State n where
  pos := play s.pos s.toMove p
  toMove := s.toMove.other
  history := insert (play s.pos s.toMove p) s.history
  lastPass := false

/-- Playing at `p` is legal if `p` is empty and the resulting grid colouring has not occurred
earlier in the game (positional superko). -/
def Legal (s : State n) (p : Point n) : Prop :=
  s.pos p = none ∧ play s.pos s.toMove p ∉ s.history

open scoped Classical in
/-- The value of the game from the state `s` under perfect play, measured as Black's score minus
White's score at the end of the game: Black maximises and White minimises over the legal turns
(a pass, or a legal move), and the game ends after two consecutive passes. -/
noncomputable def value (s : State n) : ℤ :=
  let passValue : ℤ := if s.lastPass then result s.pos else value s.pass
  let options : Finset ℤ :=
    insert passValue ((Finset.univ.filter s.Legal).attach.image fun p => value (s.move p.1))
  if s.toMove = .black then options.max' (Finset.insert_nonempty _ _)
  else options.min' (Finset.insert_nonempty _ _)
termination_by 2 * (Fintype.card (Position n) - s.history.card) + if s.lastPass then 0 else 1
decreasing_by
  · simp_all [pass]
  all_goals
    have h₁ := (Finset.mem_filter.mp p.2).2
    have h₂ : (insert (play s.pos s.toMove p.1) s.history).card ≤ Fintype.card (Position n) :=
      Finset.card_le_univ _
    simp only [move, Finset.card_insert_of_notMem h₁.2, Bool.false_eq_true, if_false] at h₂ ⊢
    omega

end State

/-- The perfect komi on the `n × n` board: Black's score minus White's score under perfect play
from the empty board. Giving White this many points of compensation makes the game end in a draw
under perfect play. -/
noncomputable def perfectKomi (n : ℕ) : ℤ :=
  State.value (State.initial n)

/-- On the `1 × 1` board no two points are adjacent, so no point reaches any colour. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem not_reaches_one (pos : Position 1) (p : Point 1) (c : Option Color) :
    ¬ Reaches pos p c := by
  rintro ⟨q, r, -, hqr, -⟩
  simp [pathGraph_adj] at hqr

/-- On the `1 × 1` board every stone is cleared as soon as it is played. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem play_one (pos : Position 1) (c : Color) (p : Point 1) :
    play pos c p = fun _ => none := by
  funext q
  obtain rfl : q = p := Subsingleton.elim _ _
  simp [play, clear, not_reaches_one]

open scoped Classical in
/-- On the `1 × 1` board, once the empty board has occurred, every move is illegal (it would
recreate the empty board), so both players can only pass. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem value_one (s : State 1) (hs : (fun _ => none) ∈ s.history) :
    s.value = result s.pos := by
  have himg : ∀ t : State 1, (fun _ => none) ∈ t.history →
      Finset.image (fun p => (t.move p.1).value)
        (Finset.filter t.Legal Finset.univ).attach = ∅ := by
    intro t ht
    rw [Finset.image_eq_empty, Finset.attach_eq_empty_iff, Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
    intro p _ hp
    exact hp.2 (play_one _ _ _ ▸ ht)
  have key : ∀ t : State 1, (fun _ => none) ∈ t.history → t.lastPass = true →
      t.value = result t.pos := by
    intro t ht h
    rw [State.value]
    simp [h, himg t ht]
  by_cases h : s.lastPass = true
  · exact key s hs h
  · rw [State.value]
    simp [h, himg s hs, key s.pass hs rfl]
    rfl

/-- On the `1 × 1` board the only legal turn is a pass, so the perfect komi is `0`. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem perfectKomi_one : perfectKomi 1 = 0 := by
  rw [perfectKomi, value_one _ (Finset.mem_singleton_self _)]
  simp [result, score, not_reaches_one, State.initial]

/-- What is the perfect value of komi? That is, what is Black's final score minus White's final
score under perfect play on the `19 × 19` board, using the Tromp–Taylor rules (area scoring,
positional superko)? Statistics from professional and computer play suggest that the answer is
`7`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 91]
theorem komi : perfectKomi 19 = answer(sorry) := by
  sorry

end Komi

Following the article's pointer to area scoring, I used the Tromp–Taylor 'logical rules' of Go exactly: area scoring (stones + empty points reaching only one colour), positional superko (a move may not recreate any earlier grid colouring, including the initial empty board and the current one), suicide allowed (own colour is cleared after the opponent's), game ends after two consecutive passes. /-!

Komi is the number of points added to White's score in the game of Go, to compensate for Black
moving first. The *perfect* komi is the value that makes a game on the standard $19 \times 19$
board end in a draw (jigo) under perfect play by both sides. Equivalently, it is the minimax
value of Black's final margin (Black's score minus White's score). Its value is not known.

The value depends on the rules. We use the Tromp–Taylor rules, a precise formulation of
area-scoring Go: Black moves first, players alternate, a turn is a pass or the placement of a
stone on an empty point that does not repeat an earlier grid colouring (positional superko),
suicide is allowed, the game ends after two consecutive passes, and a player's score is the number
of her stones plus the number of empty points that reach only her colour.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Komi (Go)](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Komi_%28Go%29)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics)

namespace Komi

open SimpleGraph

/-- The two players of Go, identified with the colours of their stones. -/
inductive Color
  | black
  | white
  deriving DecidableEq, Fintype

/-- The opponent's colour. -/
def Color.other : Color → Color
  | .black => .white
  | .white => .black

/-- The points of the `n × n` board. -/
abbrev Point (n : ℕ) := Fin n × Fin n

/-- The `n × n` grid graph: two points are adjacent if they are vertical or horizontal
neighbours. -/
def grid (n : ℕ) : SimpleGraph (Point n) := pathGraph n □ pathGraph n

/-- A colouring of the board: each point is empty (`none`) or carries a stone of a colour. -/
abbrev Position (n : ℕ) := Point n → Option Color

variable {n : ℕ}

/-- A point `p` *reaches* the colour `c` (where `none` is empty) in the position `pos` if there is
a path of adjacent points of `p`'s colour from `p` to a point of colour `c`. -/
def Reaches (pos : Position n) (p : Point n) (c : Option Color) : Prop :=
  ∃ q r, Relation.ReflTransGen (fun x y => (grid n).Adj x y ∧ pos y = pos p) p q ∧
    (grid n).Adj q r ∧ pos r = c

open scoped Classical in
/-- Clearing the colour `c`: empty all points of colour `c` that do not reach an empty point. -/
noncomputable def clear (pos : Position n) (c : Color) : Position n :=
  fun p => if pos p = some c ∧ ¬ Reaches pos p none then none else pos p

/-- Playing a stone of colour `c` on the point `p`: colour `p` with `c`, then clear the opponent's
colour, then clear one's own colour. -/
noncomputable def place (pos : Position n) (c : Color) (p : Point n) : Position n :=
  clear (clear (Function.update pos p (some c)) c.other) c

/-- The area score of the colour `c`: the number of points of colour `c` plus the number of empty
points that reach `c` but do not reach the other colour. -/
noncomputable def score (pos : Position n) (c : Color) : ℕ :=
  {p : Point n | pos p = some c ∨
    (pos p = none ∧ Reaches pos p (some c) ∧ ¬ Reaches pos p (some c.other))}.ncard

/-- Black's margin: Black's score minus White's score. -/
noncomputable def margin (pos : Position n) : ℤ :=
  score pos .black - score pos .white

/-- The state of a game: the current position, the set of all grid colourings that have occurred
so far (including the current one), the player to move, and whether the previous turn was a
pass. -/
structure State (n : ℕ) where
  /-- The current position. -/
  pos : Position n
  /-- All grid colourings that have occurred so far, including the current one. -/
  history : Finset (Position n)
  /-- The player to move. -/
  toMove : Color
  /-- Whether the previous turn was a pass. -/
  passed : Bool

/-- The initial state: the empty board, Black to move. -/
def State.initial (n : ℕ) : State n where
  pos := fun _ => none
  history := {fun _ => none}
  toMove := .black
  passed := false

/-- The state after the player to move passes. -/
def State.pass (s : State n) : State n :=
  { s with toMove := s.toMove.other, passed := true }

/-- The state after the player to move plays a stone on `p`. -/
noncomputable def State.play (s : State n) (p : Point n) : State n where
  pos := place s.pos s.toMove p
  history := insert (place s.pos s.toMove p) s.history
  toMove := s.toMove.other
  passed := false

/-- The player to move may play a stone on `p` if `p` is empty and the resulting grid colouring
has not occurred earlier in the game (positional superko). -/
def State.Legal (s : State n) (p : Point n) : Prop :=
  s.pos p = none ∧ place s.pos s.toMove p ∉ s.history

/-- The outcome preferred by the player `c` among the outcome `x` and the outcomes in `o`, where
outcomes are measured as Black's margin: Black maximises and White minimises. -/
noncomputable def Color.best (c : Color) (x : ℤ) (o : Finset ℤ) : ℤ :=
  if c = .black then (insert x o).max' (Finset.insert_nonempty x o)
  else (insert x o).min' (Finset.insert_nonempty x o)

open scoped Classical in
/-- The minimax value of Black's margin from the state `s`: the player to move chooses the best
outcome among a pass and the legal stone placements. A pass following a pass ends the game, which
is then scored. Every stone placement adds a new grid colouring to the history, so the game is
finite. -/
noncomputable def value (s : State n) : ℤ :=
  s.toMove.best (if _ : s.passed then margin s.pos else value s.pass)
    ((Finset.univ.filter s.Legal).attach.image fun p => value (s.play p.1))
termination_by 2 * (Fintype.card (Position n) - s.history.card) + (if s.passed then 0 else 1)
decreasing_by
  · simp_all [State.pass]
  · have hp := (Finset.mem_filter.mp p.2).2.2
    have h1 : (insert (place s.pos s.toMove p.1) s.history).card = s.history.card + 1 :=
      Finset.card_insert_of_notMem hp
    have h2 := Finset.card_le_univ (insert (place s.pos s.toMove p.1) s.history)
    simp only [State.play, h1]
    split <;> omega

/-- The perfect komi on the `n × n` board: Black's margin under perfect play by both sides,
starting from the empty board. -/
noncomputable def perfectKomi (n : ℕ) : ℤ := value (State.initial n)

/-- The two area scores count disjoint sets of points, so together they are at most the number of
points of the board. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem score_black_add_score_white_le (pos : Position n) :
    score pos .black + score pos .white ≤ n ^ 2 := by
  rw [score, score, ← Set.ncard_union_eq]
  · calc _ ≤ (Set.univ : Set (Point n)).ncard := Set.ncard_le_ncard (Set.subset_univ _)
      _ = n ^ 2 := by simp [Set.ncard_univ, Nat.card_eq_fintype_card, sq]
  · rw [Set.disjoint_left]
    rintro p (h | ⟨h, h1, h2⟩) (h' | ⟨h', h1', h2'⟩) <;> simp_all [Color.other]

/-- With no legal stone placement, the only option is to pass. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem Color.best_empty (c : Color) (x : ℤ) : c.best x ∅ = x := by
  cases c <;> simp [Color.best]

/-- The $1 \times 1$ board has no adjacent points. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem grid_one_not_adj (p q : Point 1) : ¬ (grid 1).Adj p q := by
  simp [grid, boxProd_adj, pathGraph_adj]

/-- On the $1 \times 1$ board no point reaches anything. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem not_reaches_one (pos : Position 1) (p : Point 1) (c : Option Color) :
    ¬ Reaches pos p c := by
  rintro ⟨q, r, -, hqr, -⟩
  exact grid_one_not_adj q r hqr

/-- On the $1 \times 1$ board every stone placement is a suicide that empties the board. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem place_one (pos : Position 1) (c : Color) (p : Point 1) :
    place pos c p = fun _ => none := by
  funext q
  obtain rfl : q = p := Subsingleton.elim q p
  cases c <;> simp [place, clear, not_reaches_one, Color.other]

open scoped Classical in
/-- On the $1 \times 1$ board, once the empty board has occurred, no stone placement is legal. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem filter_legal_one (s : State 1) (h : (fun _ => none) ∈ s.history) :
    Finset.univ.filter s.Legal = ∅ := by
  rw [Finset.filter_eq_empty_iff]
  rintro p - ⟨-, hp⟩
  exact hp (place_one _ _ _ ▸ h)

/-- On the $1 \times 1$ board, once the empty board has occurred, the player to move must pass. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem value_one (s : State 1) (h : (fun _ => none) ∈ s.history) :
    value s = if s.passed then margin s.pos else value s.pass := by
  rw [value, filter_legal_one s h]
  simp [Color.best_empty]

/-- On the $1 \times 1$ board the empty board scores $0$ for both players. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem score_empty_one (c : Color) : score (n := 1) (fun _ => none) c = 0 := by
  simp [score, not_reaches_one]

/-- On the $1 \times 1$ board the only legal turn is a pass, so the perfect komi is $0$. -/
@[category test, AMS 91]
theorem perfectKomi_one : perfectKomi 1 = 0 := by
  rw [perfectKomi, value_one, value_one]
  · simp [State.initial, State.pass, margin, score_empty_one]
  · simp [State.initial, State.pass]
  · simp [State.initial]

minus White's area score) in a game of Go on the $19 \times 19$ board under perfect play by both
sides, so that a game played with this komi ends in jigo? Here the game is played under the
Tromp–Taylor rules (area scoring, positional superko). Statistics from professional and computer
play suggest the value $7$. -/

theorem komi.variants.eq_seven : perfectKomi 19 = 7 := by

  cases c <;> simp [Board.clear, Board.place, not_reaches_one, Color.opposite] at this

/-- On the `1 × 1` board passing is the only legal move while the game is not over. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem legalMoves_one (s : State 1) (hs : ¬ s.IsOver) : s.legalMoves = {none} := by
  classical
  rw [State.legalMoves, if_neg hs, Finset.filter_false_of_mem fun p _ => not_isLegalPlay_one s p]
  simp

/-- On the `1 × 1` board the value of a state is the value after a pass. -/
@[category API, AMS 91]
theorem value_one (s : State 1) (hs : ¬ s.IsOver) : s.value = (s.play none).value := by
  rw [State.value, dif_neg hs]
  have key : ∀ m ∈ s.legalMoves, m = none := by
    simp [legalMoves_one s hs]
  have hmem : ⟨none, s.pass_mem_legalMoves hs⟩ ∈ s.legalMoves.attach := Finset.mem_attach _ _
  obtain ⟨b, c, hist, ps⟩ := s
  cases c
  · exact le_antisymm (Finset.sup'_le _ _ fun m _ => by rw [key m.1 m.2])
      (Finset.le_sup' (fun m : {x // x ∈ _} => (State.play _ m.1).value) hmem)
  · exact le_antisymm (Finset.inf'_le (fun m : {x // x ∈ _} => (State.play _ m.1).value) hmem)
      (Finset.le_inf' _ _ fun m _ => by rw [key m.1 m.2])

theorem perfectKomi_one : perfectKomi 1 = 0 := by
  rw [perfectKomi, value_one _ (by decide), value_one _ (by decide), State.value,
    dif_pos (by decide)]
  simp [State.initial, State.play, Board.margin, Board.area, not_reaches_one]

One note: the decomposition says 'the Prop is the perfect komi equals 7' but also asks for the repository's `value = answer(sorry)` shape; I followed the `answer(sorry)` shape (the statement is a question) and recorded 7 as the conjectured value in the docstring. The notes' remark that the value depends on the ruleset is correct; the ruleset choice is recorded in modeling_decisions.
modeling_decisions: Ruleset: the informal statement does not fix a ruleset, and the perfect komi can in principle depend on it (area vs territory scoring, seki handling, ko/superko variant, suicide rule). Following the article's remark that the candidate value 7 is 'under area scoring rules', the file fixes the Tromp–Taylor logical rules (area scoring, positional superko, game ends after two consecutive passes, no dead-stone agreement: dead stones must actually be captured) with the standard Chinese/AGA prohibition of suicide. Tromp–Taylor's default allows suicide; New Zealand rules also allow it. Reviewer should confirm this choice.

Perfect komi is defined as the minimax value of Black's area minus White's area (Black maximises, White minimises), rather than literally as 'the komi k such that the game with komi k is a draw under perfect play'. These are equivalent: with komi equal to the minimax value both sides can force at least a draw, and with any other komi one side forces a win. The docstring records this equivalence.

Board size fixed to the standard 19×19 (`perfectKomi 19`), as the article's discussion of komi and the value 7 concern the standard board; the model is generic in n only to allow the proven 1×1 sanity test.
Answer type is ℤ (integer komi). Under area scoring the minimax margin is an integer, so a half-integer 'tournament' komi is not what the question asks for; the article's candidate 7 is an integer.

Statement shape is `perfectKomi 19 = answer(sorry)` (the question form), with the conjectured value 7 recorded only in the docstring, per the decomposition notes and repository convention for 'determine the value' problems.

Reaching/liberties/scoring follow Tromp–Taylor verbatim: `Reaches p c` = a same-colour path from p to a point adjacent to a point coloured c; `clear c` removes c-stones not reaching empty; `area c` = c-stones plus empty points reaching c but not the opposite colour (empty points reaching both or neither colour count for nobody, e.g. seki eyes and dame).

No-suicide is formalised as: after placing the stone and clearing the opponent, clearing one's own colour changes nothing. This is equivalent to 'the new stone's string has a liberty' since only that string can lose its last liberty.

Positional superko compares the board after captures with the set of all board colourings that have occurred (history initialised with the empty board; passes do not add positions). Once the game is over (two consecutive passes) the set of legal moves is empty.

The minimax is defined by well-founded recursion on the lexicographic measure (number of board colourings not yet seen, passes remaining before the game ends); `measure_play_lt` proves every legal move decreases it, so no fuel bound is needed.

Its candidate is 7 under area scoring without seki; however, a concrete ko/superko convention and the complete underlying Go rules would still have to be fixed before this can become a Lean statement.

komi.why: A faithful statement needs a full formal model of 19×19 Go: board positions and adjacency, chains/liberties, captures, suicide legality, passes and termination, history-sensitive ko/superko legality, area scoring, the stipulated treatment/exclusion of seki, and a finite minimax score-margin evaluator for perfect play. Hard searches of Mathlib, FormalConjecturesForMathlib, and existing FormalConjectures files found no Go model. Mathlib's abstract PGame/State API only packages move relations that must already be supplied and does not provide Go rules or terminal score semantics. Introducing an uninterpreted `perfectKomi` value would be a forbidden placeholder and would not faithfully formalize the question.
